title.narrative: LFS II 2023 Annual report

description.narrative: The International Indigenous Women's Forum (FIMI) presents the Leading from the South II (LFS II) Programme’s Annual Report 2023. In the midst of implementing the second phase of LFS, 2023 has been a year of tremendous learning, which has been systematised in the 2023 Midterm Review (MTR). This report is intended to complement the MTR by highlighting the main achievements and processes implemented during 2023. This report consists of eight chapters and annexes. Following the introduction in Chapter 1, Chapter 2 summarizes the context and highlights global and regional developments and environmental changes that impacted the Indigenous Women's movement and the operation of this programme. Chapter 3 highlights the output and outcome level progress in line with the programme. Chapter 4 introduces financial progress. Chapter 5 introduces our reflections on the main cross-cutting themes, on partnership and sustainability, and on the learnings from our MTR. Chapter 6 reflects on the risks and the strategies which were adopted for their management. Chapter 7 analyses our good practices and lessons learnt during 2023. Lastly, Annex 1 addresses the reporting of the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI) and Annex 2 includes the updating of the implementating activities.

description.narrative: The International Indigenous Women’s Forum(FIMI) Ayni Fund — introduces the Leading fromthe South II (LFS II) Programme Annual Report2021. This report consists of 7 chapters and annexes. Following introduction in Chapter 1, contextanalysis in Chapter 2 highlights the external andinternal environmental changes that impact Indigenous Women (IW) movement and program operation. In chapter 3 and 4, the output and outcomelevel program progress inline with the programincluding Women’s Rights and Gender Equality(WRGE) basket indicators, and financial progressin summary explaining the changes are highlighted. Chapter 5 reflects on the risks and the adopted strategies for their management. LFS Theoryof Change (TOC), International Aid TransparencyInitiative (IATI) reporting, cross cutting issues ongender, youth, and partnership and sustainabilityare reflected in chapter 6 followed by good practices and lessons learnt in the last chapter 7.

title.narrative: Mid term report 2023

description.narrative: This is the mid-term external evaluation report of Leading from the South Phase 2 (LFS2), covering the implementation of LFS2 by the International Indigenous Women’s Forum (FIMI) during the period: January 2021 to June 2023. FIMI is one of four women’s funds that manage Leading from the South. FIMI’s budget for LFS2 is $11,832,200 USD over 5 years. The majority of these funds are being co-invested in Indigenous Women’s Organizations and networks (IWOs) who carry out projects for the advancement of Indigenous Women at the local, sub-national, national or regional levels.

A total of 61 out of 65 (94%) IWOs reported strengthened capacity to contribute to the enforcement of women’s rights andgender equality. A breakdown by region shows that the largest number of IWOs reporting such strengthened capacity is fromLAC (27), followed by Asia (21) and Africa (13), while in relative terms the share is similar across regions: Asia (95%) and LACand Africa (93% each). It is important to note that the programme targets for 2024 were exceeded, both the total target andthe targets per region, in the cases of Asia and LAC by more than double the amount. Additionally, 66 out of 67 (99%) IWOs supported by LFS II reported an increase in capacity within their organization, whetherin administration, financial management, project planning, evaluation, collaboration, and/or networking. If we break down the data by region, 29 out of 29 (100%) IWOs in LAC and 22 out of 22 (100%) IWOs inAsia, followed by 15 out of 16 IWOs (94%) in Africa reported an increase in one or more of said capacities. Overall, the data evidences the relevance and effectiveness of the support and accompaniment provided by LFS II.

In the three regions, FIMI has carried out different webinars to strengthen the capacities of members on: financial and narrative accountability and monitoring and evaluation. In addition, the members were invited to seminars on climate change and indigenous women's rights organized by FIMI. Out of 18 IWO led by women from Latin America, 12 indicated that their capacities been strengthened. In Africa, out of 23 partners, 18 have indicated that their capacities had been strengthened while in Asia, out of the 23 partners, 9 indicated that they strengthened their capabilities. It is important to highlight that targets per region were changed as informed in the MEL Plan submitted in 2021. Changes in relation to the target responds to: 1) targets values were defined before launching the IV Call, while the total number of IWOs reached in each region has been lower than expected. 2) several intermediate reports are yet pending to be delivered by partners. Disaggregation will be updated accordingly.During the Second World Conference of Indigenous Women, 9 AYNI´s partners including 5 regional/large level namely Continental Network of Indigenous Women of the Americas (ECMIA), Alianza de Mujeres Indígenas de Centro América y México (AMICAM), Network of Indigenous Women in Asia (NIWA), Asia Indigenous Women Network (AIWN) and African Indigenous Women’s Organization(AIWO) and 4 national/medium level namely National Indigenous Women’s Federation(NIWF), South Vihar Welfare Society for Tribal (ASHRAY), National Indigenous Disabled Women Association Nepal (NIDWAN) and BIWN (Bangladesh Indigenous Women Network) received grants as part of their institutional strengthening process. In this process, they were able to identify their own creative initiatives based on their needs prior to and during the conference. AYNI Partners organized the parallel sessions covering the issues of Land, territories and Resources, Climate Change, IW Resilience Power for Violence free life, Migration and COVID-19, Economic empowerment and so on in 2WCIW which was first from them over their lifetimes. Also, 13 IW representing 10 Asian AYNI Partners were panelists in 2WCIW’s different sessions. More than 100 (12%) IW from tentatively 30 AYNI Partners participated in 2WCIW conference as a whole and/or in different parallel sessions. IWO´s participation in the 2WCIW allowed them to strengthen internally, acquired greater project management and administration capacities and increased their leadership and participation in decision-making spaces to the enforcement of women's rights and gender equality. In this process, regional networks of Indigenous Women have come together to bring a “Global Political Declaration of Indigenous Women- that presents their priorities and recommendations as well as add the Indigenous woman’s voice on to the global statement. The collective document was presented to different organizations and stakeholders at national, regional and global level.
